cards.explanation: The answer is False. Wisdom doesn't hide in a quiet room. She "…calls out in the street…" "…lifts her voice in the square…" and "cries aloud" in the main concourse (Proverbs 1:20-21). Her speech happens at the city gates, right where the people are. It's open to anyone passing through, friends.

The answer is scoffers and fools. Wisdom asks, "How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?" (Proverbs 1:22). So the simple ones get company, friends. The scoffers love their scorn, and the fools hate knowledge. That's a whole crowd Wisdom is calling out.

The answer is that they've ignored her for a long time. Wisdom asks, "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" (Proverbs 1:22). Then she says they "…refused my call…" and "…neglected all my counsel…" (Proverbs 1:24-25). I think that's why she asks, friends. Her question comes after they've turned her down.

The answer is that she would have made her words known to them. Wisdom says, "If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you." (Proverbs 1:23). Those are two gifts that were ready to go, friends. All it took was repenting at her rebuke.

The answer is False. Wisdom says they "…neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction…" (Proverbs 1:25). They didn't take the counsel and skip the correction. They passed on both, friends, and that's the whole point of her complaint.

The answer is that they will call on Wisdom. She says, "Then they will call on me, but I will not answer…" (Proverbs 1:28). The very people who ignored her will be calling her name when trouble hits. Tough to hear, I know, friends. This is the part where I want to say it gently.

The answer is False, and it's a heavy one. Wisdom says, "they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me." (Proverbs 1:28). They look hard for her, and she's not found. I think that's a verse to sit with for a second, friends.

The answer is True. Wisdom says, "For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD." (Proverbs 1:29). Hating knowledge is one half, and choosing not to fear the LORD is the other. She puts them side by side in the same verse, friends.

The answer is that they get what their own choices bring. Wisdom says, "So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices." (Proverbs 1:31). Fruit is what grows from what you planted, friends. So their own way brings its own result. It's like throwing out the recipe and then being surprised by the cookies.

The answer is True, and what a way to end, friends! Wisdom finishes with, "But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil." (Proverbs 1:33). After all those hard words, she ends on a promise. Whoever listens gets safety. I love that she lands there.
